title: A new base rate changes the odds
hook: Keep evidence fixed while changing prevalence.

claims.text: With likelihood ratio 4, balanced prior odds 1 yielded posterior .8. Deployment prevalence .1 changed prior odds to 1/9 and posterior to 4/13, about .308. At prevalence .2 it became .5. This correction assumes unchanged class-conditional evidence; arbitrary shifts require more.

claims.text: At prevalence .2 with the same likelihood ratio 4, what is the posterior? Options: .5; .8; .2 Prior odds .2/.8=.25 multiply by 4 to give posterior odds 1, hence probability .5.

claims.text:
25. resampling-miscalibrates

Target / packet: ai-resampling-miscalibrates · D2. Prerequisites: ai:calibration.

Nearest / distinct payoff: calibration → say-seventy-mean-it. Calibrated training probabilities need not remain calibrated after a prior shift; this explicitly recomputes posterior odds with fixed class-conditional evidence.

Finite primary model: Same class-conditional evidence has LR 4. Balanced training prior odds 1 yields posterior=.8. Deployment positive prevalence=.1 gives prior odds 1/9, posterior odds 4/9 and probability 4/13≈.307692.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: If deployment prior .5, posterior stays .8. Assume label shift with unchanged likelihood ratio; arbitrary distribution changes need not be corrected by prior odds alone.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict whether .8 can be reused as deployment probability; recall prevalence=.2 yields odds 1 and posterior=.5.

Required observable evidence: Show prior, evidence ratio and posterior separately; no real risk estimate or universal recalibration recipe.
